comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose specific mechanisms and financial impacts of inventory write-downs, but they address different aspects of the balance sheet and operations. QCOM discloses discontinued operations related to the 'Restraint Control Systems business,' specifically noting 'write-down charges' as part of a divested segment, whereas AMD focuses on the ongoing operational risk of 'additional inventory write-downs' required if future demand assumptions change, which negatively impacts current gross margin. While QCOM treats the write-downs as part of historical discontinued operations with immaterial amounts in 2023, AMD highlights the forward-looking sensitivity of inventory valuation to market conditions.

sentences.text: Fiscal 2023 also included a gain on the sale of the Active Safety business and certain write-down charges related to the Restraint Control Systems business, the individual and aggregate amounts of which were not material.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.

comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory NRV Write-Downs Mechanics and Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company recorded inventory write-downs to NRV due to declining ASPs for DRAM and NAND; these pre-recorded charges resulted in lower subsequent cost of goods sold when the inventory was sold, with the net impact reflecting current period write-downs offset by lower costs from prior period written-down inventory.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU discuss inventory or asset write-downs, but they differ in context and accounting mechanics. QCOM discloses 'write-down charges' for the 'Restraint Control Systems business' as part of discontinued operations in fiscal 2023, noting the amounts were immaterial. MU, conversely, details the mechanics of 'inventory NRV write-downs' for active business inventory (DRAM and NAND) driven by declining average selling prices, explaining how these charges lower subsequent periods' cost of goods sold. While QCOM's write-downs are tied to a divested unit's exit, MU's are tied to current market pricing pressures on active inventory.

sentences.text: Fiscal 2023 also included a gain on the sale of the Active Safety business and certain write-down charges related to the Restraint Control Systems business, the individual and aggregate amounts of which were not material.

Inventory NRV write-downs: Our consolidated gross margin was impacted by charges in 2023 to write down inventories to their estimated NRV as a result of declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND.
As charges to write down inventories are recorded in advance of when inventories are sold, costs of goods sold in subsequent periods were lower than they otherwise would be.
